NEW DELHI: Security forces on Tuesday launched search operations at multiple locations following reports of suspected persons being spotted in Udhampur, Reasi and Kathua districts of Jammu and Kashmir, officials said.The Jammu and Kashmir Police, in coordination with the Central Reserve Police Force (CRPF), launched a cordon-and-search operation after receiving information about the movement of two suspected individuals.According to officials, the two individuals knocked on the door of one Prakash Chand in Talot village of Udhampur late Monday night and asked for food.However, the residents did not respond to the repeated knocks and alerted security forces after the suspected individuals, who were wearing shawls, left the area towards Khuban, officials said.Acting swiftly on the information, joint teams of the police and CRPF reached the village and launched a search operation, they added.Meanwhile, security forces also carried out searches in the Sadini forests of Reasi and in several villages near the International Border in Kathua’s Hiranagar sector.The operations are underway in all areas where the movement of the two suspects has been reported.
Article Summary: Jammu and Kashmir Police, in coordination with the Central Reserve Police Force (CRPF), launched a cordon-and-search operation after receiving information about the movement of two suspected individuals. Security forces also carried out searches in the Sadini forests of Reasi and in several villages near the International Border in Kathua’s Hiranagar sector.

Article Title: 'Not a single protester died': Rijiju defends Delhi police response to Jantar Mantar protests
Article Text:
Rijiju defends police response to student protests (ANI image)

NEW DELHI: Union parliamentary affairs minister Kiren Rijiju on Tuesday defended the Bihar and Delhi governments and law enforcement agencies over their handling of student protests, saying security forces managed large crowds without any casualties or serious injuries."Not a single person died; not a single person suffered a broken bone. Not even one protester is in the hospital with a serious injury. Consider the scale of this movement: thousands turned up, and so many criminals infiltrated under the guise of students," he said as cited by news agency ANI.Rijiju praised the police and administration for their handling of the protests, while contrasting it with the response to demonstrations under previous Congress-led governments."If such a movement had taken place during the Congress era, and many did, resulting in thousands of deaths, one should praise the Delhi police and the administration for handling such a massive protest without allowing even a single serious injury. Thousands actually died from gunfire during the Congress era," Rijiju said."It is the Congress that imposes an Emergency in response to protests. You might recall how many people have fallen victim to gunfire during the various movements that have taken place in this country.Even during the movement to create the state of Telangana, so many people were killed... In this movement, not a single shot was fired," he added.Rijiju said that despite the presence of thousands of protesters, including what he described as political agitators from the Aam Aadmi Party, Bhim Army and Samajwadi Party, as well as “dafli-playing agitators”, the Delhi Police used minimal force. He said force was used only when demonstrators attempted to break through barricades and march towards Parliament."Furthermore, more than half the people, whether from the Aam Aadmi Party, the dafli-playing agitators, the Bhim Army, or the Samajwadi Party, came and incited others to violence; yet, not a single casualty occurred," Rijiju added.On the Gen-Z movement and its demand for education reforms, Rijiju said the Narendra Modi-led NDA government remained committed to the welfare of the country’s youth.He also called for strict judicial action against those responsible for examination leaks and reiterated the government’s zero-tolerance stance on violence during public protests."We respect the students' sentiments. The Prime Minister introduced such a good law and took step after step, promising to work for their future," Rijiju said.The remarks came amid student protests in Bihar over alleged examination irregularities and the NEET paper leak controversy.Clashes were reported between protesters and police in Siwan on July 25 following stone-pelting, after which police used tear gas and lathi charges to disperse the crowd. An AK-47 firing incident was also reported during the unrest.The remarks come weeks after the CJP called off its 37-day protest at Jantar Mantar on July 25, following the resignation of then Education Minister Dharmendra Pradhan and assurances on some of the protesters’ other demands.The agitation was centred on the NEET paper leak issue and drew students and young volunteers from across the country, along with support from opposition leaders. Activist Sonam Wangchuk joined the protest on June 28 and began an indefinite hunger strike. He was later shifted to Safdarjung Hospital after his health deteriorated.The protest also saw police action on July 20 when demonstrators attempted to march towards Parliament. The Congress and other opposition parties later raised the issue in Parliament, contributing to disruptions during proceedings.
Article Summary: Union parliamentary affairs minister Kiren Rijiju defends police response to student protests. He says security forces managed large crowds without any casualties or serious injuries. Comments come amid student protests in Bihar over alleged examination irregularities and NEET paper leak controversy.

Article Title: Supreme Court bars CBI, ED from filing report on Rahul Gandhi's assets
Article Text:
File photo: Rahul Gandhi

If claim is so serious, why did agencies need HC prod: SC

NEW DELHI: Supreme Court Monday barred CBI ED or any agency from filing any report on any probe into the alleged disproportionate assets of leader of opposition in Lok Sabha Rahul Gandhi before Allahabad HC, which had directed the two central agencies to probe allegations in a PIL on his alleged illegal wealth.Arguing for Rahul and challenging the July 20 order of HC’s Lucknow bench, senior advocate Kapil Sibal told a bench of CJI Surya Kant and Justices Joymalya Bagchi and V Mohana that the HC had adopted a process which is “completely unknown to law” in passing the impugned orderKapil Sibal said HC did not even seek Rahul Gandhi’s response and permitted a witch-hunt without questioning the locus standi of the petitioner, Vignesh Shishir, an RSS/BJP worker.Appearing for CBI, additional solicitor general S V Raju said, “CBI has done nothing yet. We are only verifying the complaint. We have not registered even a preliminary enquiry. The allegations are very serious. We are inquiring into it.” Sibal said, “CBI can do what it likes. We are not concerned with it.”Justice Bagchi said, “You (CBI) did not do it on your own. Suo motu action we would have understood. Why did you need the prodding of high court to investigate? If it is so serious, why did the agencies keep quiet and need impetus from HC?”The bench issued notices to Shishir, CBI, ED, UP Police, Union ministry of home affairs, CBDT and Serious Fraud Investigation Office and said, “Meanwhile, no report shall be submitted by CBI or ED or any other authority to the HC pursuant to its July 20 order.”Sibal sought a stay on proceedings before HC, leading the bench to request HC to defer the scheduled Aug 20 hearing till further orders. Appearing in person, Shishir spoke in favour of HC’s procedure, and said the matter was still in the preliminary enquiry stage where the accused cannot have a say.Raju said, “As far as the allegations are concerned, if they make out a cognisable offence, it stands on a different footing. We are yet to lodge an FIR. What action is to be taken has not yet been considered.”CJI Kant said, “On our understanding of the law, police or any probe agency, if they have prima facie material, they can register a case, investigate it, and can proceed against anyone. No permission is required from the accused. But what appears to us, subject to assistance from both sides, is that if the court wants to issue a direction, it is expected to follow principles of natural justice.”Raju said it was not required in a criminal case. Sibal interjected and said, “The enthusiasm of the agencies is clear.” Raju retorted, “Facts may be wrong or right. But if they are right, it is a gross case of disproportionate assets.” Sibal said these were sealed cover, in-chamber proceedings and asked how they got reported in newspapers.In his plea, Rahul said, “Since 2024, Shishir, who it appears from public reporting is a member of BJP — a party whose politics and ideology the petitioner (Rahul) and his party (Congress) vehemently contests — has instituted multiple proceedings before different forums, including successive PILs on petitioner’s alleged foreign citizenship, criminal proceedings seeking registration of an FIR...”
Article Summary: If claim is so serious, why did agencies need HC prod: SC. Sibal said HC did not even seek Rahul Gandhi’s response and permitted a witch-hunt without questioning the locus standi of the petitioner, Vignesh Shishir, an RSS/BJP worker.

Article Title: 'Remove bulletproof glass or I won't speak': Ex-officer recalls PM Modi's demand on I-Day 2014
Article Text:
PM Modi said, 'if this stays in front of me, I would not be able to address the citizens'," the officer recalled.

Former defence secretary RK Mathur has recalled how Prime Minister Narendra Modi insisted on removing the bulletproof glass barrier from the Red Fort before delivering his first Independence Day address as Prime Minister in 2014.Speaking about the episode, Mathur said he and the then Director of the Intelligence Bureau (IB) had briefed Modi about the security arrangements ahead of August 15. The officials had specifically discussed the bulletproof glass barrier placed in front of the Prime Minister."Me and the Director of Intelligence Bureau (IB), went to PM Modi for a briefing before August 15 because it was his first Independence Day where he would address the country from the ramparts of the Red Fort (as the Prime Minister).""During that conversation we explained him (PM Modi) that there is a barrier in front of him which is the bulletproof glass. PM Modi said, 'if this stays in front of me, I would not be able to address the citizens'," he told news agency IANS.Mathur said security officials initially opposed removing the shield because of the risks involved. The location offers a wide view of the surrounding area, including buildings in Chandni Chowk, making security arrangements particularly sensitive."From our side, this was naturally a security issue. As people know, the entire Chandni Chowk area is visible from there (Red Fort) where there are many buildings. That is why, from a security standpoint we urged the Prime Minister to rethink his decision. However, PM Modi clearly stated that if this (bulletproof shield) is not removed, he will not address."The former defence secretary said the security team eventually agreed to Modi's demand and removed the glass barrier just hours before the Independence Day ceremony."Due to this, I and the director of IB changed our standpoint and decided to remove the bulletproof glass. This glass shield was then removed on the intervening night of August 14 and 15, at about 2 am," Mathur added.The episode was recalled as Modi once again departed from established security protocol during the 80th Independence Day celebrations on Saturday, when he met schoolchildren, NCC cadets and 'My Bharat' volunteers at the Red Fort after his address.During the interaction, a young girl approached Modi and bent down to touch his feet. As she did so, her cap slipped from her head and fell to the ground.Modi immediately bent down, picked up the cap and placed it back on the girl's head. The gesture drew smiles and applause from the children and people around them.
Article Summary: Former defence secretary RK Mathur has recalled how Prime Minister Narendra Modi insisted on removing the bulletproof glass barrier from the Red Fort. Mathur said he and the then Director of the Intelligence Bureau (IB) had briefed Modi about the security arrangements ahead of August 15.

Leader of opposition in the Lok Sabha Rahul Gandhi on Monday criticised Prime Minister Narendra Modi over the cancellation of the UGC-NET examinations He accused the government and the National Testing Agency ( NTA ) of failing to ensure a fair and reliable examination process.Rahul said the examinations, held between June 22 and 30, were cancelled nearly two months after they were conducted. He added that thousands of candidates who had prepared for the exams, paid application fees and travelled to examination centres would now have to appear again in September."Modi ji, look at what your NTA has just done. UGC-NET exams for Sociology, English and Commerce were held between 22 and 30 June. Nearly two months later, NTA has cancelled all three because it set faulty papers and repeated old questions. Thousands of candidates who prepared for years, filled forms, paid the fees, travelled to distant centres, must now do it all again in September. NTA makes the mistake but the student serves the sentence," Rahul Gandhi said in a post on X.Rahul also questioned whether the question papers had been leaked before the examinations and demanded accountability from the NTA leadership.He said the resignation of former education minister Dharmendra Pradhan should be followed by action against those responsible at the testing agency."I said this in Kota, in Dehradun, in Prayagraj, and I will keep saying it - this is no longer an education system. It is an extraction machine. It takes your money, your years, your mental health, and your confidence and returns nothing. Not even a job. NTA still won’t answer the real question - were these papers leaked before the exam?" Rahul added.Rahul further alleged that the NTA had not taken responsibility for the cancellation and questioned whether those responsible would be held accountable.Addressing candidates who will have to retake the exams in September, Rahul said they were “not the problem” and accused the Centre of creating an examination system that had failed students."Dharmendra Pradhan’s resignation was the first step, not the last. NTA’s leadership must be held accountable too. To every student sitting this exam again in September - you are not the problem. PM Modi built a system that cannot run an exam and then blames the students who take it. Your years are being stolen and we will not stop until PM Modi answers for it," Rahul added.NTA on Sunday acknowledged multiple errors and repeated questions in the UGC-NET papers for English, Commerce and Sociology, and announced fresh examinations for all three subjects on September 9 and 10.The agency said a committee constituted after receiving “several complaints” found “many factual, typographical, translation errors” in the papers. These included misspelt names of prominent scholars, distorted book titles, incorrectly worded questions, grammatical and punctuation errors, and non-standard terms for established concepts. The committee also found a “significant number” of questions that had appeared in previous examinations.The NTA said the extent of the errors meant the papers did not meet the standards of a fair and error-free examination. It said the issues could not be resolved simply by dropping defective questions after the answer-key challenge process, making fresh examinations necessary.The decision came hours after the agency released provisional answer keys for 84 of the 87 UGC-NET subjects, while withholding the keys for English, Commerce and Sociology. The June examinations were held nearly seven weeks before the decision to conduct the re-tests.
Article Summary: Rahul Gandhi accuses government and National Testing Agency of failing to ensure fair and reliable examination process. UGC-NET exams for Sociology, English and Commerce were held between 22 and 30 June. Nearly two months later, NTA has cancelled all three because it set faulty papers and repeated old questions.

Article Title: NTA admits errors, orders fresh NET for 3 subjects
Article Text:
Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Insightful Agree Disagree Skeptical Concerning Promising Worth Reading Big Development Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

NEW DELHI: National Testing Agency (NTA) on Sunday acknowledged that the UGC-NET papers in English, Commerce and Sociology had multiple errors and repeated questions, and said the defects were too extensive to be addressed simply by dropping questions after the answer-key challenge process. It has ordered fresh examinations for all three subjects.The re-tests will be held on September 9 and 10. English will be conducted from 9am to noon on September 9, Commerce from 3pm to 6pm the same day, and Sociology from 9am to noon on September 10. No additional examination fee will be charged.The decision came hours after NTA released provisional answer keys for 84 of the 87 UGC-NET subjects but withheld the keys for these three papers, nearly seven weeks after the June examination.NTA said a committee set up after receiving “several complaints” found “many factual, typographical, translation errors”, including misspelt names of prominent scholars, garbled book titles, wrongly worded questions, grammatical and punctuation mistakes and non-standard terms used for established concepts. The committee also found repetition of a “significant number” of questions previously asked.The agency said papers carrying defects of this extent did not meet the standards of a fair and error-free examination and that the problems could not be corrected merely by dropping questions after challenges were received.TOI had on July 1 reported complaints over the Sociology and English papers. Sociology candidates alleged that the June 30 paper contained spelling and grammatical errors, mangled names of well-known thinkers, poor Hindi translations and questions apparently unrelated to the prescribed syllabus. Some also alleged that parts of the paper appeared AI-generated.Candidates had pointed out that “Ritzer” appeared as “Putzer”, “Parsons” as “Parsow”, “Ghurye” as “Ghunye” and A R Desai as “A K Desai”, among several other errors.The English paper had also come under scrutiny after candidates alleged that 67 of its 150 questions were identical to questions asked in the 2024 examination, with even the sequence of answer options reportedly unchanged. Complaints over repetition were subsequently raised in Commerce as well.The episode comes two years after the June 2024 UGC-NET was cancelled a day after it was held following inputs received by UGC from the National Cyber Crime Threat Analytics Unit under the home ministry indicating that the integrity of the examination may have been compromised. The test was subsequently conducted afresh.The current re-examination will, however, not hold up results in the other 84 subjects. NTA said their results would be declared as scheduled and JRF allocation and certificates for Assistant Professor and PhD eligibility would not be delayed.For assistant professor eligibility, NTA said the number qualifying would be 6% of candidates who appeared in the June test or the re-test, whichever is higher.
Article Summary: National Testing Agency says papers in English, Commerce and Sociology had multiple errors and repeated questions. NTA says defects were too extensive to be addressed simply by dropping questions after the answer-key challenge process. It has ordered fresh examinations for all three subjects on September 9 and 10.

What is Save America Act

US President Donald Trump on Tuesday praised India’s election system and called for the passage of the SAVE America Act, which seeks to require proof of citizenship and voter identification in US elections.In a post on Truth Social, Trump cited a recent conversation involving Chief Election Commissioner Gyanesh Kumar and highlighted India’s use of photo identification for voters.Trump said, "Earlier this month, India’s Chief Election Commissioner, Gyanesh Kumar, asked our Administration, How can you have Elections in the US without a valid Photo ID?"Referring to the last general election, Trump said, "India's last Election had 646,000,000 Voters! Less than 1 per cent voted by mail, and every single Voter had to have a VALID Photo Identity Document."Trump also renewed his call for Congress to pass the SAVE America Act, saying, "We need to pass THE SAVE AMERICA ACT, now!"According to the White House, the proposed legislation seeks to ensure that only US citizens are eligible to vote in federal elections. "American citizens and only American citizens should decide American elections," the White House said, describing the bill as a "common sense, bipartisan bill."The legislation would require voters to provide valid identification and proof of US citizenship when registering to vote in federal elections. It also proposes limiting mail-in voting to certain circumstances, including illness, disability, military service and travel, according to news agency ANI.The White House said the bill would further require states to remove non-citizens from federal voter rolls. "If you want to register to vote in the United States, you have to be a citizen in the United States," it said.The administration also compared US election practices with those of other countries, arguing that the US has weaker voter-identification safeguards. "India and Brazil tie voter ID to a biometric database, while the United States largely relies on self-attestation for citizenship," the White House said.The bill was introduced in Congress on January 29. Trump has repeatedly backed the SAVE America Act, arguing that stricter voter-ID and citizenship requirements are necessary to strengthen election security.The SAVE America Act is a proposed US law aimed at tightening voting rules in federal elections. Article Title: Devendra Nath Mahto: 'Huge victory for Jharkhand': Student leader Mahto ends 16-day hunger strike after Soren govt accepts demands
Article Text:
Student leader Mahto ended his fast in Ranchi in the presence of state ministers Dipika Pandey Singh and Irfan Ansari.

Soren govt scraps JSSC-CGL, TDPL exams

Govt announces more exam cancellations, probes

Three student leaders end hunger strike

Students seek withdrawal of cases

Rahul Gandhi backs students

NEW DELHI: Student leader Devendra Nath Mahto on Monday late night ended his 16-day hunger strike after the Jharkhand government announced the cancellation of the JSSC-CGL examination and all examinations conducted by TDPL, calling the decision a “huge victory for Jharkhand”.Mahto ended his fast in Ranchi in the presence of state ministers Dipika Pandey Singh and Irfan Ansari. He thanked chief minister Hemant Soren, Congress leader Rahul Gandhi, ministers and others who supported the students' agitation.“Today marks the 16th day of the hunger strike; this struggle began on July 2nd,” Mahto said.He said the government had taken a “bold step” by cancelling the JSSC-CGL examination even though its recruitment process had reached the joining stage and some candidates had already secured appointments.“I thank the Jharkhand government for showing the courage to make such a significant decision, canceling an exam was a massive challenge,” he said.“Today marks a huge victory for Jharkhand. While I am now suspending my protest, my struggle for reform will continue,” Mahto added.He called for stringent reforms to prevent paper leaks and irregularities, saying every examination should be monitored and audited.“If this requires the Legislative Assembly to enact new laws or necessitates a constitutional amendment, then so be it.Every examination must be monitored, every examination must be audited, and there must be a clear certificate for every examination and at every stage; we will continue to struggle for this,” he said."Consequently, we are announcing the suspension of our peaceful protest today. While we will continue to struggle for further reforms. I thank the Jharkhand government for showing the courage to make such a significant decision—canceling an exam was a massive challenge. It was not an easy call, given that the recruitment process for the JSSC CGL examination had already reached the joining stage and many students had likely already secured their positions. Yet, considering the critical situation, the government took this bold step for the students......" he added.CM Hemant Soren said the decision was taken at a special Cabinet meeting after considering the concerns raised by the protesting students.“Today, we held a special Cabinet meeting to bring this matter to a conclusion. After considering all aspects and finding solutions to the issues, we have decided to cancel all examinations conducted by TDPL, the results published by TDPL, and the selection or participation of any candidates through TDPL. All activities undertaken by TDPL in this regard have also been cancelled,” Soren said.The government also decided to cancel the JSSC-CGL examinations. Soren said the government viewed the protesting students as young people concerned about their future and promised greater transparency in recruitment reforms.“I do not consider these young people to be different groups. They are all concerned about their future. The government will move ahead with complete transparency on reforms,” he said.He said an existing standard operating procedure (SOP) should have prevented the alleged irregularities and promised further improvements based on suggestions from stakeholders.“There is already an SOP for conducting examinations, and if it had been followed, these irregularities would not have occurred. Nevertheless, further improvements will be made based on suggestions received,” Soren said.The government has also opened a portal for students, teachers and parents to submit suggestions on examination reforms.Jharkhand minister Dipika Pandey Singh said the government would also cancel the 14th JPSC examination and backlog examinations.She said the government would write to the Enforcement Directorate to investigate alleged financial misappropriation, while the CID probe would be monitored by the judiciary.Meanwhile, the Jharkhand CID began searches at the JSSC office in Ranchi as part of its investigation into alleged irregularities in recruitment examinations. CID ADG Manoj Kaushik said the searches were being conducted in connection with the allegations.The state probe agency has so far arrested 20 people in the case, including former JPSC chairman L Khiangte.Minister Irfan Ansari said Mahato, Umme Habiba and Rahul Kranti voluntarily ended their hunger strike after the government accepted their demands.“Just now, Devendra Mahato, Umme Habiba, and Rahul Kranti voluntarily took the initiative to end their hunger strike. We facilitated the end of their hunger strike. We helped them break their fast by giving them juice,” Ansari said.He said the agitation had formally ended following efforts by Dipika Pandey Singh and Jairam Mahato.“The government has accepted all their demands; these were significant demands and a major issue. However, in the interest of the youth, our Chief Minister took such a historic decision,” Ansari said.He added that, “all three are healthy; there are no issues—their blood pressure and blood sugar levels are normal. From the information I have received, everything is fine.”Student leader Umme Habiba said students wanted all legal action against protesters withdrawn and their right to peaceful protest respected.“Any legal action, whether an FIR or any proposed measure registered against the students should be withdrawn, and the right to peaceful, democratic protest must be respected,” she said.She also sought the reinstatement of suspended official Santosh Mastana and action to expedite the closure or withdrawal of CID Case No. 025.“I am struggling for the rights of Jharkhand's candidates, a fair recruitment system, and the security of their future,” Habiba said.Congress leader Rahul Gandhi had earlier urged Soren to personally meet representatives of the protesting students and address their concerns. In a letter dated August 14, Rahul described the agitation as peaceful and the students' demands as legitimate. He also backed their right to protest and said Congress stood with students raising concerns over paper leaks and irregularities in the recruitment system.Jharkhand Congress in-charge K Raju also urged the chief minister to resolve the issue at the earliest.The state government has announced several measures aimed at making recruitment examinations more transparent and secure.These include a time-bound annual examination calendar, technology-secured examinations, timely publication of answer keys and OMR sheets, and multi-level accountability in the recruitment process.The government has also invited suggestions from students, teachers, educationists and parents on reforms to the examination system.The agitation had intensified earlier this month when thousands of job aspirants marched towards the Jharkhand assembly in Ranchi. Police used lathis, tear gas and water cannons to disperse protesters after they breached barricades, according to reports.

Article Title: Indian handle quoted by Netanyahu & US: How a false claim fooled the world
Article Text:
Hawkish narrative got significant boost from a fake quote.

Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Insightful Agree Disagree Skeptical Concerning Promising Worth Reading Big Development Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

Tehran's alleged effort to develop nuclear weapons has been the key reason cited by US President Trump and Israel govt for the war on Iran. In recent weeks, amid stop-start peace efforts, the hawkish narrative got a significant boost from a fake quote first posted by an Indian X handle, which then raced through Tel Aviv-Washington political and diplomatic circles, right up to PM Benjamin Netanyahu and White House."Alert," the account, @RealBababanaras, posted on Aug 5, "While world is expecting peace, IRGC Chief Ahmad Wahidi again threatened -'There will be no talk on Enriched Urenium (sic) or nuclear weapons, as long as US & Israel are owning nuclear weapons, we will keep working on it for national security. If they dispose, we will dispose." This reference was to Brig Gen Ahmad Vahidi, head of Iran's Revolutionary Guard, and one of Iran's powerful military figures.In less than two hours, another India-based account, @Im_Ritikaa, posted a paraphrased version in Hindi.Neither cited any sources. An Israeli news outlet, YNet, and The New York Times have since reported that there is no evidence this statement was ever made by Vahidi. But the posts on Indian X had already found resonance in Israeli media. By the afternoon of Aug 5, Mossad Commentary, a prominent Israeli account (but not affiliated with Israel's intelligence agency, Mossad), published the fake statement with a comment: "The regime is not preparing to abandon its nuclear ambitions.It is buying time. There will be no deal." The post was seen more than 300,000 times by Aug 17.About half an hour later, Israeli broadcaster Channel 14 English posted it as news, with its own comment: "This is the first time an Iranian official has admitted to developing a nuclear bomb." The post had almost 450,000 views at the time of filing this report.By evening, Israel PM Netanyahu's son Yair had reposted both. From there, the claim made a short leap to Netanyahu's podium. At a state ceremony in Jerusalem honouring the family of Theodor Herzl, the founder of modern political Zionism, Netanyahu presented it as fact. "Today we heard Revolutionary Guards commander Vahidi explicitly declaring Iran's intention to continue to develop nuclear weapons," he said. "Continue! That is what he said. Well, as prime minister of Israel, I too am determined to continue preventing Iran from possessing nuclear weapons."Within minutes, US ambassador to UN, Mike Waltz, reposted the claim - as did American Conservative commentator Mark Levin and Republican senator Rick Scott later. By the night of Aug 5, it had made its way to Fox News (which clarified later the claim had been "taken out of context and amplified").The actual Vahidi comment, it said, was based on one made in 2025 - that Iran's position on nuclear weapons had been transparent, and Iran was "ready to do whatever it deems necessary in response to their (the US's and Israel's) repeated aggression".So, how did an anonymous Indian account become the cited source for the Israeli information ecosystem? This was, incidentally, not the first time material had travelled between @RealBababanaras and Mossad Commentary. In at least two posts this year after Iran war began - one reporting continuing explosions in Iran after a US strike as evidence that missiles were stored there, and another which reported a US strike on an alleged uranium-enrichment and nuclear research facility - it cited @RealBababanaras as the source.As early as April, a month and a half after the US and Israel began air strikes in Iran, @RealBababanaras posted Tehran was preparing for its "first official nuclear test within weeks". Days later, @FalconUpdatesHQ, which has over 150,000 followers and claims in its bio to be based in Kerala, echoed that, claiming Iran was preparing to conduct its first official nuclear test within a month. The claim was recycled by @Im_Ritikaa in May.Earlier this year, Yonatan Hassidim, CEO of an Israeli firm that monitors and analyses online and social activity, said in an Israeli parliamentary hearing that about 70% of accounts sharing Netanyahu's posts in their sample were not Israelis at all. "That is to say, an Indian account shares a video of the Israeli prime minister speaking in Hebrew. Within 12 seconds, it has already understood that this item interests it - it apparently understands Hebrew - and shares it," he had said, before citing the example of an Indian account that "tweets more than 165,000 tweets a year"."So these are high volumes, and this is some kind of average account," he added, "We have seen ones with 300,000 a year and more as well."The loop is still active. On Aug 17, when US president Donald Trump posted on Truth Social the "no. 1 goal is, and always will be, that Iran cannot have, in any way, shape, or form, a Nuclear Weapon", @RealBababanaras repackaged this for its audience as a reaction "after Iran refused handing over enriched uranium and halting nuclear programme".
Article Summary: Hawkish narrative got significant boost from a fake quote. Fake quote was first posted by an Indian X handle, which then raced through Tel Aviv-Washington political and diplomatic circles, right up to PM Benjamin Netanyahu. An Israeli news outlet, YNet, and The New York Times have since reported that there is no evidence this statement was ever made by Brig Gen Ahmad Vahidi.

Article Title: Jharkhand protests: Soren govt cancels JSSC-CGL exam, tests held via TDPL; to set up reforms panel - key points

Government announces recruitment reforms

NEW DELHI: Amid the ongoing protest by job aspirants over alleged irregularities in recruitment examinations, Jharkhand chief minister Hemant Soren on Monday announced the cancellation of the JSSC-CGL exam and all tests conducted by outsourced agency TDPL since 2014.The move came after the agitation, led by the JPSC-JSSC Reforms Manch, demanded a CBI probe into alleged irregularities and cancellation of the JSSC-CGL examination. Most of the demands made by the students have now been accepted by the Jharkhand government.Student leader Devendra Nath Mahato thanked the Jharkhand government and CM Hemant Soren for accepting the students' demands and said the ongoing probe was targeting those involved in examination irregularities.He said that he would soon reach the protest site in Ranchi to break his hunger strike.He said the students would continue to support efforts to remove corruption from the examination system and would cooperate with the government in the ongoing reform process."We extend our heartfelt thanks to all the students, parents, members of the media, the police administration, and especially the Jharkhand government and CM Soren for supporting and cooperating with this movement.We express our gratitude for taking the students' issues seriously and fulfilling our demands; most importantly, the investigation is being conducted meticulously, and every corrupt individual involved is being apprehended. They are making a concerted effort to reach the true kingpins behind these gangs," said Mahato.Mahato also said they would support the government's investigation into alleged examination irregularities but stressed that they wanted a system that would prevent paper leaks and other irregularities in the future.The student protest in Ranchi over alleged irregularities in examinations conducted by the Jharkhand Public Service Commission and Jharkhand Staff Selection Commission (JSSC) had entered its 24th day on Monday.Jharkhand chief minister Hemant Soren said that the state government has decided to cancel all examinations conducted by TDPL, the results published by the company, and the selection or participation of candidates through TDPL, amid the ongoing student protest over alleged irregularities in recruitment exams.The government also decided to cancel the JSSC-CGL examinations.Soren said the decision was taken at a special Cabinet meeting after the government considered the concerns raised by protesting students and sought to bring the issue to a conclusion.“Today, we held a special Cabinet meeting to bring this matter to a conclusion. After considering all aspects and finding solutions to the issues, we have decided to cancel all examinations conducted by TDPL, the results published by TDPL, and the selection or participation of any candidates through TDPL. All activities undertaken by TDPL in this regard have also been cancelled,” Soren said.Speaking about the protesters at Jaipal Singh Stadium, Soren said the government viewed them collectively as young people concerned about their future and promised greater transparency in recruitment reforms.“I do not consider these young people to be different groups. They are all concerned about their future. The government will move ahead with complete transparency on reforms,” Soren said.He said an existing standard operating procedure (SOP) for conducting examinations should have prevented the alleged irregularities, but added that the government would make further improvements based on suggestions from stakeholders.“There is already an SOP for conducting examinations, and if it had been followed, these irregularities would not have occurred. Nevertheless, further improvements will be made based on suggestions received,” Soren said.The chief minister said a portal had also been opened for students, teachers and parents to submit suggestions, which would subsequently be shared with experts for consideration.The Jharkhand CID on Monday began raids at the JSSC office in Ranchi as part of its investigation into alleged irregularities in various recruitment examinations.CID ADG Manoj Kaushik told PTI that the searches were being conducted in connection with the allegations. The state probe agency has so far arrested 20 people in the case, including former JPSC chairman L Khiangte.A delegation of protesting JPSC-JSSC candidates was scheduled to meet the state government's committee for another round of talks. This is the seventh round of discussions between the two sides, with earlier meetings failing to break the deadlock.The protesters have been demanding comprehensive reforms in the JPSC and JSSC recruitment systems, a CBI probe into alleged irregularities and cancellation of the JSSC-CGL examination. Six protesters continue to remain on hunger strike.Jharkhand minister Dipika Pandey Singh said the government would cancel the 14th JPSC examination and backlog examinations.She also said the government would write to the Enforcement Directorate to investigate alleged financial misappropriation, while the CID probe would be monitored by the judiciary. Pandey said the government was committed to reforms aimed at safeguarding the future of students.Singh and Irfan Ansari said the government remained committed to addressing the students' demands through dialogue.Ansari accused the BJP of attempting to "hijack" the student movement, while Pandey alleged that the opposition was using the protesters to target the state government. The BJP, meanwhile, has backed the students' demand for a CBI probe and criticised the government's handling of the agitation.Congress leader Rahul Gandhi has urged chief minister Hemant Soren to personally meet representatives of the protesting students and take steps to resolve their remaining concerns.In a letter dated August 14, Rahul described the students' protest as peaceful and their demands as legitimate. He also backed the right to peaceful protest and said Congress stood with students raising concerns over paper leaks and irregularities in the education system.Congress is part of the ruling JMM-led alliance in Jharkhand.Also read: Rahul Gandhi writes to ally Hemant Soren over Jharkhand student protests Jharkhand Congress in-charge K Raju said Rahul Gandhi and the party stood firmly with the protesting job aspirants and urged Soren to resolve the issue at the earliest.Raju said Congress leaders had met the chief minister and appealed to him to address the students' concerns. He said the four-member committee appointed by Soren would hold another meeting with the protesters on Monday.The protesters have said they will not call off the agitation unless the government takes concrete action on their demands.The JPSC-JSSC Reforms Manch has also called for broader changes in the recruitment system. The protesters had earlier announced plans to gherao the chief minister's residence on August 20 and appealed to students from across Jharkhand to gather in Ranchi.The agitation intensified on August 10 when thousands of job aspirants marched towards the Jharkhand Assembly in Ranchi. Police used lathi-charge, tear gas and water cannons to disperse protesters after they breached barricades, according to reports.The confrontation further escalated the standoff between the student groups and the state government.The agitation has now entered its 24th consecutive day, with six protesters still on hunger strike. The protesters have indicated that they will continue the stir unless the government's assurances translate into concrete action.Student leader Devendra Mahto, who has now been on hunger-strike for 15 days, says he hopes that fresh rounds of talks with the state government would bring positive results.With the latest talks taking place against the backdrop of the CID raids and growing political pressure, Monday's discussions could prove crucial in determining whether the prolonged standoff finally moves towards a resolution.The Jharkhand government has announced several measures aimed at making recruitment examinations more transparent and secure. These include a time-bound annual examination calendar, technology-secured examinations, timely publication of answer keys and OMR sheets, and multi-level accountability in the recruitment process.The government has also launched a consultation seeking suggestions from students, teachers, educationists and parents on reforms to the examination system.
Article Summary: Jharkhand chief minister Hemant Soren announced the cancellation of the JSSC-CGL exam and all tests conducted by outsourced agency TDPL since 2014. The move came after the agitation, led by the JPSC-JSSC Reforms Manch, demanded a CBI probe into alleged irregularities. Most of the demands made by the students have now been accepted by the government.

NEW DELHI: Congress MP Imran Masood on Monday said that he would respect the national song but would not sing it, citing his constitutional right to practise his religion.His statement came amid row over the recitation of Vande Mataram involving grand old party high-command Sonia Gandhi , Rahul Gandhi and Mallikarjun Kharge.While speaking on the Vande Mataram row, Masood told news agency ANI, "I cannot worship anyone except Allah. All devotees have been provided every possible facilities by the temple administration. Darshan continues at the temple."The temple administration said the large turnout was linked to Nag Panchami coinciding with Monday during the holy month of Shravan.The Nagchandreshwar Temple, located atop the Mahakaleshwar Temple, opens only once a year for 24 hours on the occasion of Nag Panchami. Thousands of devotees gather to seek the blessings of Lord Nagchandreshwar during the annual opening.While the temple administration denied any incident inside the temple, reports emerged of devotees being injured in the area around Harsiddhi Chauraha.A woman whose son was admitted to hospital told ANI that he was injured after being caught under a barricade while heading towards the temple."This occurred at Harsiddhi Chauraha. He came under a barricade when he was going for a darshan at Nath Chandreshwar Mandir. A stampede had broken out there. Nobody helped him. Only one man carried him here..." she said.One of the injured, Sagar, said he had been waiting in the queue for several hours before the incident occurred."I was in the queue at Mahakal Mandir for the darshan. After seven to eight hours, I reached Harsiddhi Chauraha. We stood there for two hours. The crowd was swelling and since it was time for the aarti, we were stopped there. Suddenly, the barricades were opened and a stampede broke out," he said.He said he was trapped and injured after the barricades collapsed."The tent fell, and all the barricades fell too. Both of my legs were caught under the barricade. One of my legs is fractured. The arrangements were really poor at the temple. Nobody helped me. Only one man came and helped me; he carried me to a health camp, from where I was taken away in an ambulance," Sagar was quoted as saying by news agency ANI.Chaos was also reported near Bada Ganesh Temple, Neelkanth Square and along the route from Kark Raj Parking towards the Harsiddhi entrance.Officials subsequently reached the affected areas and worked to restore order as devotees continued to arrive at the temple complex.The incident occurred amid one of the year's biggest religious gatherings in Ujjain, with the simultaneous observance of Nag Panchami and Sawan Somvar drawing lakhs of devotees to the Mahakaleshwar temple.
Article Summary: Several devotees injured after stampede-like situation breaks out near Mahakaleshwar Temple complex in Madhya Pradesh's Ujjain. Rumour about electric current in barricades triggered panic among devotees heading towards the Shri Nagchandreshwar Temple. Some barricades reportedly broke as the crowd surged. Temple administration denies any chaos or stampede had occurred inside the temple.

Article Title: Cauvery row: Supreme Court asks Karnataka to comply with water release directions to Tamil Nadu
Article Text:
SC tells Karnataka to follow CWMA directions

The Supreme Court on Monday directed Karnataka to comply with the Cauvery Water Management Authority’s (CWMA) directions on the release of Cauvery water to Tamil Nadu.The court posted for hearing on August 24 Tamil Nadu’s plea seeking directions for the release of water.It said the matter could be taken up then, allowing an updated status on the water released by Karnataka to be placed before the court.Tamil Nadu approached the Supreme Court on August 3, saying it was not receiving its allocated share of Cauvery water despite the state facing a rain-deficient year.The state government alleged that both the quantity recommended for release by the Cauvery Water Regulation Committee and the water actually supplied by Karnataka were well below its requirement.Tamil Nadu said recent rainfall in the catchment areas of the KRS and Kabini reservoirs had increased the volume of water due to the state.According to the state government, the proportionate share due at Biligundlu should be 26.954 TMC.At a meeting on July 28, the Cauvery Water Regulation Committee directed Karnataka to release 3,500 cusecs of water to Tamil Nadu for 15 days from July 29. Tamil Nadu, however, said the actual flow recorded at Biligundlu on the Karnataka-Tamil Nadu border ranged between 158 and 550 cusecs from July 29 to August 2.The state government also cited storage levels in Karnataka’s four reservoirs. As of August 3, the combined storage in the Krishna Raja Sagara, Kabini, Harangi and Hemavathy reservoirs stood at 77.537 TMC, according to a Tamil Nadu government statement.Tamil Nadu said the available storage indicated that Karnataka could release the state’s due share without difficulty.
Article Summary: Tamil Nadu approached the Supreme Court on August 3, saying it was not receiving its allocated share of Cauvery water. The state government alleged that both the quantity recommended for release and the water actually supplied by Karnataka were well below its requirement. The court posted for hearing on August 24 Tamil Nadu's plea seeking directions for the release of water.

Article Title: Chidambaram says he is 'proud to be a dimaagi Naxal'; BJP hits back
Article Text:
Sudhanshu Trivedi, P Chidambaram

Chidambaram's response to PM Modi

BJP-Congress clash over Naxalism

NEW DELHI: BJP national spokesperson Sudhanshu Trivedi on Monday hit back at Congress leader P Chidambaram over his ‘dimagi Naxal’ remark, questioning the Congress' position on Naxalism by invoking former Prime Minister Manmohan Singh's 2006 assessment of the threat.Trivedi said PM Modi had raised the issue in his Independence Day address and questioned Chidambaram's decision to embrace the label a day later."PM Modi raised a very important topic of 'Dimagi Naxal' on Independence Day. We are surprised that within 24 hours of this, Congress leader P Chidambaram has said that he is proud of being a 'Dimagi Naxal,'" Trivedi said.His remarks came a day after Chidambaram responded to PM Modi's Independence Day speech by saying, "I am proud to be a dimagi naxal!"Trivedi then cited a statement made by Manmohan Singh on April 13, 2006, when the former prime minister described Naxalism as a major internal security challenge.Also read - ‘Proud to be a dimagi naxal’: P Chidambaram hits back at PM Modi "I want to remind Congress and P Chidambaram that on 13th April 2006, former PM Dr Manmohan Singh said, "It would not be an exaggeration to say that the problem of Naxalism is the single biggest internal security challenge ever faced by our country"," Trivedi said."I want to ask the Congress - who was right, Dr Manmohan Singh or P Chidambaram?" he added.Chidambaram's remarks came after PM Modi, in his Independence Day address from the Red Fort, warned about what he described as a ‘dimagi naxal’ or Naxal mindset.PM Modi said armed Naxalism was nearing its end but cautioned that people with an ideological Naxal mindset could continue to pose a threat."Even if these naxals are gone, but the 'dimagi naxal' (people with naxal thinking), are looking for an opportunity, looking to see ways of violence, and trying to drag the country to a wrong path," PM Modi said.He also urged people to "identify and isolate" those he accused of seeking opportunities to promote violence and unrest.Chidambaram's response followed criticism from other Congress leaders over the Prime Minister's remarks. Congress general secretary Jairam Ramesh accused PM Modi of reviving labels such as "urban naxal" and "dimagi naxal" to target political opponents."First, you make derogatory remarks--calling them 'Urban Naxals' or 'Mental Naxals'--but later, you accept the very demands your political opponents were making," Ramesh said, according to ANI.The BJP has defended PM Modi's remarks and sought to frame the debate around internal security and ideological challenges, while the Congress has questioned the use of terms such as ‘dimagi Naxal’ against political critics.Trivedi's attack specifically sought to contrast the Congress' current response with the position taken by the Congress-led UPA government under Manmohan Singh.PM Modi had also said that the government had prioritised eliminating Naxalism since coming to power in 2014, claiming that decades of Maoist violence had damaged the lives and aspirations of young people and resulted in the deaths of security personnel."In 2014, when you gave us the opportunity we had decided that we will rid the country of naxalism, and today I am happy to announce that naxalism does not have even the strength for breathing," PM Modi said.The remarks have triggered a wider political debate over the distinction between armed Naxalism, ideological opposition and dissent, with opposition parties accusing the government of using the terminology to target its critics.The BJP has maintained that the term refers to individuals or ideological networks that it believes indirectly support or promote anti-national narratives.
Article Summary: BJP national spokesperson Sudhanshu Trivedi hit back at Congress leader P Chidambaram over his ‘dimagi Naxal’ remark. He questioned the Congress' position by invoking former Prime Minister Manmohan Singh's 2006 assessment of the threat. Chid Ambaram responded to PM Modi's Independence Day speech by saying, "I am proud to be a dimagi naxal!"

Article Title: Trump's foreign policy: Strongmen on speed dial, allies and partners on notice
Article Text:
TOI correspondent from Washington

: Forget bombing Iran to end it as a civilization, US President Donald Trump on Sunday dropped bombshells on America's allies and partners, including India, to send a disquieting message: good ties with Washington may no longer guarantee its support in return.Within hours of each other, Trump warmly endorsed a new defence pact linking Saudi Arabia, Pakistan and Turkey while ordering a substantial reduction in US-South Korean military exercises, explicitly invoking his “very good relationship” with North Korean dictator Kim Jong Un. Taken together, the moves suggest a foreign policy increasingly organized around personal relationships, immediate transactional demands, and affinity for strongmen rather than the institutional logic of long-standing alliances.“Very happy to see” Saudi Arabia, Turkey and Pakistan sign the Mecca Joint Defence Agreement, Trump wrote on Truth Social, praising it as a step toward countries defending themselves “in a more meaningful way.” The pact commits the three to regard an armed attack on one as an attack on all and envisages deeper military cooperation.For India, the optics are particularly uncomfortable despite the much ballyhooed personal rapport between Trump and Modi.Pakistan’s military chief Asim Munir has cultivated an unusually close relationship with Trump and his family on the strength of a crypto outreach; Saudi Crown Prince Mohammed bin Salman and Turkish President Recep Tayyip Erdogan have likewise established strong personal channels with the president. Trump’s enthusiastic embrace of a pact involving Pakistan therefore contrasts sharply with Washington’s traditional effort to deepen India’s role as a democratic counterweight to China.The Mecca pact is not explicitly directed against India, and New Delhi has responded cautiously, saying it is studying its implications for national security and regional stability. Nor does Trump's endorsement amount to abandoning India. But the symbolism is unmistakable: Washington is applauding a new security architecture that is concerning to India even as he has virtually turned his back on Quad and unloaded against BRICS.The South Korea decision is even more startling. On Sunday, Trump said he had ordered Defense Secretary Pete Hegseth to “substantially reduce” the annual Ulchi Freedom Shield exercises, which began Monday and involve about 18,000 South Korean troops. Trump complained about their cost, Seoul’s refusal to participate in US military action against Iran and, most revealingly, their supposed hostility toward a North Korea that he described as “unthreatening and respectful” because of his “very good relationship” with Kim.The irony is difficult to miss. South Korea is a treaty ally; North Korea is widely seen as a kooky nuclear-armed dictatorship that has supplied Russia with weapons and troops for its war in Ukraine. The exercises are designed precisely to maintain readiness against Pyongyang and now include training for drones, cyberwarfare, electronic warfare and GPS disruption.Richard Fontaine, president of the Center for a New American Security, called the administration's Asia policy increasingly incoherent, warning that excessive inconsistency could encourage countries to accommodate potential adversaries rather than rely on America. Victor Cha and Andy Lim of CSIS had earlier identified the underlying problem: Trump evaluates allies through transactional metrics -- defense spending and trade balances -- creating pressure for greater payments while threatening diminished security commitments.The pattern extends well beyond Asia. Neighbors Canada and Mexico has been subjected to extraordinary pressure from Trump, while European allies have faced tariffs, troop withdrawals and repeated questions about the value of NATO. Several foreign-policy analysts have expressed alarm at the developments, describing them as an increasingly transactional and damaging approach to America's traditional alliance system.Trump's defenders argue that this is not abandonment but burden-sharing: uncertainty is supposed to force allies to spend more on their own defense. MAGA activist Laura Loomer, a fringe element who is now an influential voice in Washington, offered precisely that kind of justification, arguing that South Korea should have helped Trump with Iran and that America's alliances depend on the unique personal authority Trump commands abroad.Yet that defense inadvertently makes the central problem clearer: if alliances and partnerships depend on personal ties with one president, they cease to be that in the traditional sense. The danger is not merely that Washington may lose friends; it is that friends may conclude they need insurance against Washington itself.Foreign policy mavens say that is the paradox of Trump's “America First” diplomacy : by making American protection conditional and personal, he may encourage allies from Seoul to New Delhi to Ottawa to Brussels to become more self-reliant and less dependent on America. Once allies and partners learn that lesson, they warn, rebuilding trust may prove considerably harder than destroying it.
Article Summary: US President Donald Trump on Sunday dropped bombshells on America's allies and partners, including India. Trump warmly endorsed a new defence pact linking Saudi Arabia, Pakistan and Turkey. He also ordered a substantial reduction in US-South Korean military exercises. Taken together, the moves suggest a foreign policy increasingly organized around personal relationships.

Article Title: Karnataka BJP MLA's daughter booked for 'assaulting' woman cop over temple entry queue
Article Text:
Police registered an FIR after a woman sub-inspector alleged that the BJP MLA's daughter tried to bypass the queue and assaulted her. (Photo: Instagram)

NEW DELHI: The daughter of Karnataka BJP MLA B Suresh Gowda was booked for allegedly abusing and assaulting a woman police sub-inspector following an argument at a temple in Mandya district in Karnataka, police said on Friday.The incident took place on August 12 at the Maramma Temple in Ukkada village during Bhima Amavasya celebrations, news agency PTI reported.According to the complaint filed by the woman police officer, she was deployed at the temple for security duty when Aishwarya , the MLA's daughter, allegedly sought permission to enter the sanctum without waiting in the queue.The police officer alleged that she asked Aishwarya to wait to avoid inconvenience to other devotees. According to the complaint, Aishwarya then identified herself as the daughter of an MLA and questioned why she was being stopped.The argument allegedly escalated, with Aishwarya abusing the officer and hitting her on the head. The complainant also alleged that she was threatened and prevented from performing her official duties.Based on the complaint, the Kyathanahalli police registered an FIR under relevant sections of the Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita (BNS), including charges related to assaulting a public servant, causing simple hurt, intentional insult and criminal intimidation, a senior police officer said.However, the case has taken another turn, with Aishwarya filing a counter-complaint against the police officer.Police said an inquiry into her allegations has been initiated, but no FIR has been registered on the basis of her complaint so far. Further action will depend on the findings of the inquiry.Speaking to reporters, Tumakuru Rural MLA B Suresh Gowda apologised for his daughter's conduct and said that anyone found guilty should face legal consequences."If she has committed a mistake, it is wrong. Whoever has done the mistake should face the consequences under the law," he said.The BJP legislator said his daughter had visited the temple with her two young children and had requested permission to enter briefly because waiting in the queue could have caused inconvenience.He also claimed that another person had been allowed to enter ahead of her, prompting his daughter to question the decision.While acknowledging that the argument had escalated, Gowda said his daughter should have shown greater restraint, particularly because she comes from a political family."I apologise on behalf of my daughter if she has made a mistake," he said.The MLA also called for a departmental inquiry into the incident and urged authorities to take action against anyone found responsible.
Article Summary: Karnataka BJP MLA B Suresh Gowda's daughter booked for allegedly abusing and assaulting a woman police sub-inspector. Incident took place on August 12 at the Maramma Temple in Ukkada village during Bhima Amavasya celebrations. Aishwarya Gowda allegedly sought permission to enter the sanctum without waiting in the queue.

Article Title: Pakistani minister in Balochistan province escapes armed attack on convoy
Article Text:

Balochistan home minister Mir Ziaullah Langove escaped unharmed after armed attackers targeted his convoy in Mastung district on Friday, injuring six people, including three police personnel.The attack took place in the Khad Kocha area as Langove was travelling from Quetta to Kalat, Balochistan government spokesperson Shahid Rind said."Six people were injured in the attack, but the minister remained unhurt and the convoy has returned to Quetta," Rind said.All six injured people suffered bullet wounds, according to a senior police official. Three of them were police personnel, with two reportedly in serious condition. They were taken to a hospital in Quetta for treatment.The attack has raised fresh security concerns in Khad Kocha, an area that has repeatedly come under attack in recent weeks.According to officials, this was the fourth attack on travellers along the same highway since last month. Insurgents have repeatedly targeted people travelling through the area despite a major security operation carried out following the earlier incidents.Security forces have now sealed off the area and launched a search operation to locate those responsible for the latest attack.The incident adds to the continuing security challenges in Balochistan, where armed insurgent groups have carried out attacks against security forces and civilians.
Article Summary: Balochistan home minister Mir Ziaullah Langove escaped unharmed after armed attackers targeted his convoy. The attack took place in the Khad Kocha area as Langove was travelling from Quetta to Kalat. All six injured people suffered bullet wounds, according to a senior police official.

Article Title: Volhynia massacres: Russia using WWII to plant discord between Ukraine and Poland?
Article Text:
Polish officials and researchers say Moscow has sharply increased online messaging around the Volhynia massacres.

How Russia is 'exploiting' the Volhynia dispute

The facts may be real, but the narrative can still be manipulated

Ukraine fatigue creates fertile ground for the campaign

Russia is being accused of using a painful chapter in the history of Poland and Ukraine to deepen tensions between the two countries, as Warsaw and Kyiv remain divided over the killings that took place during World War 2.Polish officials and researchers say Moscow has sharply increased online messaging in Poland around the Volhynia massacres, while also using the issue to fuel anger against Ukrainians living in the country.The campaign has largely played out on social media, with much of the content appearing in Polish. Analysts say the aim is not always to create completely false stories, but to amplify real disputes in ways that can deepen existing divisions.The historical dispute centres on the Volhynia massacres between 1943 and 1945. Poland says Ukrainian nationalists killed around 100,000 Poles during the violence, while thousands of Ukrainians were also killed in retaliatory attacks.Tensions over the issue increased after Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenskyy named an army unit after insurgents linked to the massacres. Polish president Karol Nawrocki, who is from the political right, responded by stripping Zelenskyy of a major Polish honour in June.Polish deputy digital minister Pawel Olszewski said the disagreement was quickly followed by a surge in Russian messaging across social media and Russian media platforms, including Telegram.Research by the state-backed Polish Institute of International Affairs found that Polish-language anti-Ukrainian content on X, Facebook, Instagram, TikTok and YouTube rose by more than 250% after Zelenskyy's decision.Filip Bryjka of PISM said much of this increase appeared to have been artificially boosted through bots, creating the impression that anti-Ukrainian sentiment was spreading rapidly.Analysts say one reason this type of campaign is difficult to detect is that it does not necessarily depend on completely fabricated information.Instead, genuine events and historical grievances can be repeatedly highlighted and framed in ways that encourage anger towards a particular group."The event is real, but the interpretation is imposed by an external actor," said Wojciech Pokora, an analyst at Info Ops Poland Foundation.Moscow has rejected the accusations. The Russian embassy in Warsaw said Russia does not interfere in relations between other countries."The Russian Federation does not interfere in the relations between other states," the Russian embassy in Warsaw said in an emailed statement, adding that accusations about Russia spreading disinformation to undermine support for Ukraine are baseless.The issue has gained greater importance because Poland remains one of Ukraine's strongest supporters in its war against Russia, but public backing for Ukraine has weakened.An IBRiS poll published last month found that 33.6% of respondents said their attitude towards Ukrainians had worsened following the latest dispute linked to the World War Two killings.Another IBRiS survey found that support for continuing military assistance to Ukraine had fallen to 52%, compared with 78% in 2022.Researchers caution that declining support for Ukraine cannot be blamed entirely on Russian influence.Poland is home to an estimated 1.8 to 1.9 million Ukrainian migrants, while disagreements over grain imports and the unresolved legacy of the Volhynia killings have also contributed to public frustration.Olszewski said the Russian messaging had "fallen on fertile ground".Meanwhile, hostility towards Ukrainians in Poland has reportedly increased, prompting prime minister Donald Tusk to call for an end to xenophobic attacks.The issue could become even more politically significant ahead of Poland's 2027 parliamentary elections. Polling suggests Tusk's pro-European government could struggle to retain power, while support for the far-right has been growing.That makes the Volhynia dispute more than a historical argument. For Poland, it touches on a painful national memory. For Ukraine, it is part of a complicated shared history with its neighbour. And for Russia, Polish analysts argue, the disagreement offers an opportunity to deepen divisions between two countries that have otherwise stood together against Moscow.
Article Summary: Polish officials and researchers say Moscow has sharply increased online messaging around the Volhynia massacres. Campaign has largely played out on social media, with much of the content appearing in Polish. Analysts say aim is not always to create completely false stories, but to amplify real disputes in ways that can deepen existing divisions.

Article Title: Zeeshan Siddique gets death threat from Portugal number, caller claims Godara gang link
Article Text:
NCP leader Zeeshan Siddique reported receiving a death threat from a Portugal-based number (File photo)





MUMBAI: National Congress Party leader and MLC Zeeshan Siddique filed a complaint soon after he arrived in Mumbai on Friday morning after a fresh threat he received while he was in London at 2.36 (which was 7.06 am IST).Bandra police registered a non-cognisable (NC) offence against an unknown person based on an audio threat he received on August 12.Siddique received the threat audio clip from a Portugal number.Siddique confirmed TOI that Bandra police registered an NC based on the complaint he submitted."The audio threat that lasted 1.29 minutes was received on my WhatsApp number by the same person who identified himself as Zeeshan Akhtar. My sister filed the first NC on August 6 while I was abroad. Now, the death threat audio clip was sent directly to me using Portugal number. In November 2025, we filed the writ and soon my security cover was reduced from eight cops to two. Also, there was 22 cops deployed at my residence which was reduced to zero," he said.The person who sent the audio threat dared Siddique to go and file a police complaint himself instead of sending his sister forward to file the complaint and threatened he will the one to kill him.TOI extracts the transcript of the threat audio which states, "Listen here, Zeeshan Siddique, this is Zeeshan Akhtar speaking. Listen to me carefully: I am going to kill you. Before I even touch your father... well, I had already assigned a team to the task two years ago, back when I was in police custody, got it?""Brother, everyone I’ve killed, I did so openly. Now, your end has come. Don't push your sister to the forefront; if you have the guts, go file the complaint yourself. I know everything; I’m aware of every detail. You might not die today or tomorrow, but within a year, you will definitely die. I have no problem with your money and I am not threatening you for money. The person claimed that he object to my illegal business and for which he will kill me. He threatened: 'You will die, and I am the one who will kill you'," the transcript stated further.The first threat compaint was filed by Siddique's sister Arshia on August 6. She was in the Bombay High Court (HC) for the hearing of a writ petition filed for initiating action against a builder whose role is suspected behind their father's murder."This is not coincidence. Both the threats are being made when the dates for the writ petition was nearing," he said.DCP (West Zone-2) Mohit Garg confirmed about the fresh NC registered on complaint from Siddique.A case of criminal intimidation involving severe threats, such as threatening death and grievous hurt was registered against unknown person.
Article Summary: Siddique received the threat audio clip from a Portugal-based number. Bandra police registered a non-cognisable (NC) offence against an unknown person. The person who sent the audio threat dared Siddique to go and file a police complaint himself instead of sending his sister forward to file the complaint.

Article Title: ‘We can drive them crazy’: Rahul Gandhi takes aim at PM Modi, Amit Shah

Rahul addressed a conclave of Rachnatmak Congress
