In a statement suggesting that students’ protest and the Parliament session washout have the ruling BJP at a loss for strategy, Congress leader Rahul Gandhi said “we” will not relent till PM Narendra Modi and home minister Amit Shah quit power under pressure. Party chief Mallikarjun Kharge said Modi and Shah will destroy the country and not leave anything for the coming generations. Kharge said Gujarat produced visionary leaders, but now “these two” are ruining everything.Rahul said the country is witnessing a fight between “those who give orders and those who want to express themselves”, adding that the country has started expressing itself after a lot of people behaved like “cowards” against the combine of RSS-BJP for a long time.“Our job is to make India express itself and break that order,” the Congress leader said, adding “we will drive them crazy”.Rahul and Kharge addressed a conclave of Rachnatmak Congress, that seeks to create a common political strategy with non-Congress platforms of people’s struggle.Rahul said Modi is unable to sleep at night while Amit Shah, who was eulogised as Chanakya, did not come to Parliament for 20 days. “Because for the first time, they are feeling India’s expression. They realise this country will not stop expressing itself.It will break the RSS order.”“Till Modi and Shah give their resignations, they will not be able to sleep, we will keep them awake,” he said.He lashed out at the RSS as a “bunch of jokers”, and said the organisation has been reduced to being an instrument of big capital like Adani and Ambani, far from its original base of small businesses.The leader of opposition said Modi has messed up India’s national security and foreign policy, the latter because of the ignorant idea that he is making friends with the world leaders and foreign policy is about hugging them. He said Modi thought foreign leaders were his friends, and “they caught him”. He said India squandered a great opportunity presented by the Iran war to play the mediator, and the role was usurped by Pakistan.In what had the large audience from across the country in splits, Rahul illustrated Modi’s hugging by giving a bear hug to Rachnatmak Congress chief Sandeep Dikshit - who in turn asked Rahul jokingly “if he had thought he was hugging Italian PM Meloni”, and by enacting other practical jokes. He also cited a childhood anecdote of how then PM Indira Gandhi did not take seriously the US administration’s attempt to flatter her via the then First Lady.
Article Summary: Rahul Gandhi said ‘we’ will not relent till PM Narendra Modi and home minister Amit Shah quit power under pressure. Party chief Mallikarjun Kharge said Modi and Shah will destroy the country and not leave anything for the coming generations. Rahul and Kharge addressed a conclave of Rachnatmak Congress.

Article Title: F-16 fighter jet crashes in Turkey during training flight, pilot safe
Article Text: A Turkish Air Force F-16 fighter jet crashed during a training flight in the northwestern province of Yalova on Wednesday, Chinese state news agency Xinhua reported.According to the defence ministry, the pilot survived the crash after safely ejecting from the aircraft.In a statement posted on social media, the ministry said the aircraft went down during a routine training mission and that the pilot safely bailed out before the crash.The exact cause of the accident will be determined following a detailed investigation, the ministry added.A large number of ambulances and medical rescue teams were dispatched to the crash site following the incident, local media reported.Live footage broadcast by Turkish news channel NTV showed a fireball and thick black smoke rising from the wreckage, visible from several locations across the province.
Article Summary: A Turkish Air Force F-16 fighter jet crashed during a training flight in the northwestern province of Yalova. According to the defence ministry, the pilot survived the crash after safely ejecting from the aircraft. A large number of ambulances and medical rescue teams were dispatched to the crash site.

Article Title: Dan Scavino, Natalie Harp, Walt Nauta: 3 aides were allowed with Trump when he was moved into a catering truck during Turkey emergency
Article Text:
Dan Scavino, Natalie Harp and Walt Nauta are the closest aides allowed inside the catering truck that hid President Donald Trump in Turkey.

Who is Dan Scavino?

Who is Natalie Harp?

Who is Walt Nauta?

No cabinet officials were allowed inside the catering truck, inside which President Donald Trump was snuck away last month in response to a potential Iranian assassination threat in Turkey. Apart from some low-ranking aides, only three individuals were allowed inside the truck, as they are believed to be the closest to the president: Dan Scavino, the White House deputy chief of staff; Natalie Harp, Trump's assistant and Walt Nauta, the director of Oval Office operations. Washington Post reported that neither Marco Rubio nor Pete Hegseth nor Stephen Miller were allowed inside the truck that took TrumpThe catering truck moved under concealment from the Air Force One aircraft to a smaller Air Force C-32A before flying to Britain separately.Dan Scavino has been serving as the White House deputy chief of staff in the second Trump administration but his history with Trump dates back to 1992, when he worked as a caddie at a New York country club that Trump later purchased and turned into Trump National Golf Club Westchester. After graduating from college, Scavino worked his way up to become the golf club's general manager.He joined Trump's 2016 presidential campaign and went on to serve throughout the entire first Trump administration as White House Director of Social Media and later Deputy Chief of Staff for Communications.During that time, he was particularly known for managing Trump's personal social media presence and online strategy. He remained a central advisor at Mar-a-Lago following the 2020 election, worked as a senior official on the 2024 campaign, and returned to senior White House leadership upon Trump taking office again in 2025.Natalie Harp is an American political aide and former television presenter who serves as Executive Assistant to the President in Donald Trump's second White House administration. She is the one who handles the president's daily schedule and is always spotted with him. Known colloquially among campaign staffers and media outlets as Trump's "human printer," Harp earned a reputation for constantly accompanying him with a portable printer to feed him printed news articles, polls, and favorable commentary. In her role as executive assistant, she remains a member of his inner circle, assisting with his daily schedule and managing dictation for his social media accounts.Walt Nauta is a close political aide to Donald Trump and currently serves in his second White House administration as Deputy Assistant to the President and Director of Oval Office Operations. Nauta spent 20 years in the U.S. Navy, reaching the rank of Senior Chief Petty Officer. During his military career, he was assigned to the Presidential Food Service and eventually became a White House valet during Trump's first presidency. In that role, he acted as a personal assistant and "body man," handling day-to-day tasks like fetching beverages and managing travel details.After Trump left office in 2021, Nauta retired from the Navy and joined Trump's personal staff at Mar-a-Lago, continuing to work as his primary executive assistant and political aide. He later drew widespread national attention when he was indicted alongside Trump in June 2023 in the federal classified documents case, where prosecutors accused him of helping move and conceal boxes of sensitive materials.
Article Summary: No cabinet officials were allowed inside the catering truck, inside which President Donald Trump was snuck away last month in response to a potential Iranian assassination threat in Turkey. Dan Scavino, the White House deputy chief of staff; Natalie Harp, Trump's assistant and Walt Nauta, the director of Oval Office operations, are believed to be the closest aides to the president.

Article Title: Thailand visit, Suu Kyi access: Can Myanmar’s Min Aung Hlaing win political legitimacy?
Article Text:
Min Aung Hlaing in Thailand; Aung San Suu Kyi with ICRC official

Min Aung Hlaing's ascent to power

Significance of Aung San Suu Kyi

Why Thailand visit matters for Min Aung Hlaing - and how Bangkok differs from ASEAN

Can regional engagement help Min Aung Hlaing’s legitimacy push?

Min Aung Hlaing’s continuing legitimacy challenge

Myanmar President Min Aung Hlaing made a two-day state visit to Thailand last week, in a trip that carried significance beyond routine diplomacy. He remains internationally isolated because, in his earlier role as supreme commander of Myanmar’s armed forces, he led the 2021 coup that overthrew the elected civilian government. He subsequently ruled as head of the junta for five years before formally assuming the presidency.That visit to Thailand coincided with another significant development in Myanmar. Aung San Suu Kyi , the former leader whose government was ousted in that coup, was allowed to receive a visitor. On August 3, Suu Kyi met Arnaud de Baecque, the International Committee of the Red Cross' (ICRC) resident representative in her country.Naypyidaw also released photographs of the meeting—the first official images of the former State Counsellor in years.Was the close timing of the two developments just a coincidence? For Min Aung Hlaing, who came to power by overthrowing an elected government rather than through the ballot box, both developments could be part of a broader effort to build political legitimacy and gain wider international acceptance.During his visit to Thailand, the 70-year-old former military leader sought to reassure his host, Thai Prime Minister Anutin Charnvirakul, that Myanmar was “returning to democracy.”"Myanmar has now re-established itself on the path to democracy and is moving toward a better future," Min Aung Hlaing told Charnvirakul.The remarks stood in sharp contrast to the circumstances of his rise to the presidency. His claim that Myanmar is on a “democratic path” also comes against the backdrop of a bloody civil war triggered by the coup that brought him to power.According to the Assistance Association for Political Prisoners, an independent organisation that documents arrests and casualties linked to the Myanmar civil war, more than 8,200 civilians had been killed and 31,645 people arrested by the regime's security forces as of August 5.Besides, the parliamentary elections under Min Aung Hlaing in late 2025 and early 2026 were also widely criticised as “neither free nor fair” as the army-backed Union Solidarity and Development Party swept the elections, winning 232 of the 263 contested seats in the lower house and 109 of 157 seats in the upper house. Ahead of the presidential election in April—Myanmar's first since 2018—he resigned from the military and was subsequently elected president.However, his transition to the presidency did little to ease international scepticism. Major democracies withheld congratulations following his victory.For Myanmar, Aung San Suu Kyi’s significance extends beyond her role as the head of the country’s first democratically elected civilian government in 50 years and the military’s toppling of her administration.For many inside and outside Myanmar, the 1991 Nobel Peace Prize laureate remains the country's most recognisable symbol of democratic rule and civilian legitimacy.In 2022, Suu Kyi was sentenced to 33 years in prison on a series of charges that her supporters and rights groups described as “politically motivated” and intended to prevent her return to politics. Later, her sentence was reduced to 27 years and, in April, to 18 years, while she was transferred to house arrest.Against this backdrop, the meeting with the ICRC representative was significant because it marked the first confirmed contact between Suu Kyi, 81, and an independent international organisation since her house arrest. It was also her first confirmed communication with the outside world since she wrote a letter to her son from prison in early 2024.Sreeparna Banerjee, an Associate Fellow at the Observer Research Foundation (ORF), agreed that both developments could be seen as part of Myanmar’s broader effort to “manage its international image,” but said it cannot be assumed that the moves were directly linked.“The timing is noteworthy, but it would be difficult to establish a direct connection between the two developments at this stage… Access to Aung San Suu Kyi after a prolonged period of isolation could signal some limited openness, while Min Aung Hlaing’s high-profile visit to Thailand demonstrates Myanmar’s attempt to expand diplomatic engagement,” Banerjee, whose work focuses on Myanmar and Thailand, told The Times of India.For Min Aung Hlaing, the bigger challenge remains turning such diplomatic engagement into wider political legitimacy and international acceptance.According to Banerjee, the visit was important for Min Aung Hlaing because it offered him a degree of political normalisation.“Being received at the highest level by an ASEAN neighbour allows him to project the image of a leader whose government is once again engaging with the region rather than remaining diplomatically isolated,” she said.Significantly, while Thailand and Myanmar are both ASEAN member states, Bangkok’s approach towards Naypyidaw differs from that of the rest of the 11-nation bloc of Southeast Asian states.Thailand has continued to engage with Myanmar despite ASEAN barring Min Aung Hlaing from its top-level meetings over the non-implementation of the Five-Point Consensus agreed with the grouping after he seized power.On this, Banerjee observed that the real value of Bangkok’s “bridge” diplomacy — acting as a bridge between Myanmar and ASEAN — would depend on whether Thailand can use it to encourage some meaningful progress on the Five-Point Consensus.Additionally, ASEAN is yet to recognise the results of Myanmar’s 2025–26 parliamentary elections. The bloc has also repeatedly called for Suu Kyi’s unconditional release, renewing the demand after her meeting with the ICRC official. The regime rebuffed this call too.For its part, Thailand has described its approach vis-à-vis Myanmar as one of “calibrated re-engagement” aimed at keeping dialogue open while responding to “realities on the ground.” Bangkok has also argued that Myanmar is essential to ASEAN unity and regional stability, provided it remains peaceful and stable.In addition to being barred from top-level ASEAN summits, Min Aung Hlaing faces Western sanctions over his role in toppling Suu Kyi’s government, the subsequent civil war, and the alleged persecution of the Rohingya minority in the Rakhine province.The Thailand visit was his fourth overseas trip since becoming president, following visits to India, China, and Laos. India was the only democratic country among the four destinations, underscoring the limited engagement he has so far had with democratic governments.Despite this, and close ties with Russia, he has remained largely isolated internationally.So, can his engagement with Thailand and his wider regional outreach — help him in his bid for greater international recognition and acceptance?Sreeparna Banerjee, the ORF Associate Fellow, suggested that even regional acceptance remains uncertain at this stage, despite such engagement being an important part of Myanmar’s quest for political legitimacy.“Naypyidaw appears determined to engage on its own terms rather than fully follow the ASEAN framework. Thailand's outreach may create space for dialogue, but whether this translates into wider regional acceptance remains uncertain,” she explained.She also highlighted that uncertainty over Myanmar’s regional acceptance stems in part from the fact that Singapore will take over the ASEAN chairmanship in 2027. The city-state has repeatedly called for full implementation of the Five-Point Consensus.This underscores the scale of the challenge facing Min Aung Hlaing in his bid for wider acceptance.For a leader who rises to power as Min Aung Hlaing did, securing international recognition is likely to remain a gradual and difficult process.The regime’s refusal to release Suu Kyi, a global icon, further complicates that effort.Engagement with neighbouring countries can provide an important opening, but broader recognition often depends on how other governments assess the resulting political situation. Yet for Min Aung Hlaing, this remains the only option to secure recognition.For now, engagement with Thailand may offer Min Aung Hlaing some diplomatic space, but whether it can translate into legitimacy for him remains uncertain.
Article Summary: Myanmar President Min Aung Hlaing made a two-day state visit to Thailand last week. He remains internationally isolated because, in his earlier role as supreme commander of Myanmar’s armed forces, he led the 2021 coup that overthrew the elected civilian government. He subsequently ruled as head of the junta for five years before formally assuming the presidency. Aung San Suu Kyi, the former leader whose government was ousted in that coup, was allowed to receive a visitor.

Article Title: Tech millionaire Bryan Johnson hits back at ‘eating disorder’ claims: ‘I’ve achieved perfect discipline’
Article Text:
What Bryan Johnson said

Data‑driven accountability

Read Byran Johnson’s complete post here

‘People say I have an eating disorder.

Because I've achieved perfect discipline of what I eat. It's taken me years to achieve this mastery.

Yet the reaction is to call it a disorder.

Should a straight A student get some Bs, Cs and Ds to avoid having a grade disorder?

Should an NBA player miss some shots to avoid having a shooting disorder?

Should an engineer introduce some bugs in the code to avoid having a code disorder?

We celebrate mastery of craft in other domains. Why not what we put into our bodies?

I'm accountable to my biomarkers and change the protocol according to the data.

Like any quest for mastery, this one can steer into unhealthy territory. But self control over food intake is as worthy of respect as mastery of any other craft.’

Anti-aging influencer and tech millionaire Bryan Johnson has reignited a long-running public debate over his relationship with food, posting on X that he rejects being told he has an eating disorder, arguing instead that what critics see as pathology is actually years of disciplined mastery over what he eats. “People say I have an eating disorder. Because I've achieved perfect discipline of what I eat. It's taken me years to achieve this mastery,” Johnson wrote, questioning why mastery in food intake is often pathologised when excellence in other fields is celebrated.In the post, Johnson wrote that people accuse him of having an eating disorder because he has achieved what he describes as perfect discipline in his diet, something he says took years to build. He questioned why that discipline gets labeled a disorder rather than celebrated as skill, drawing comparisons to other domains where extreme consistency is praised rather than pathologized: a straight-A student isn't told to get some Cs to avoid a "grade disorder," he argued, an NBA player isn't told to miss shots to avoid a "shooting disorder," and an engineer isn't told to introduce bugs to avoid a "code disorder." He said he holds himself accountable to his biomarkers and adjusts his health protocol based on data, while acknowledging that any pursuit of mastery, including this one, can tip into unhealthy territory. Even so, he maintained that self-control over food intake deserves the same respect as mastery of any other craft.Johnson emphasised that his approach is not rigid dogma but biomarker‑driven. He said he continually adjusts his protocol based on measurable health data, treating food intake as a craft worthy of respect. “Like any quest for mastery, this one can steer into unhealthy territory. But self‑control over food intake is as worthy of respect as mastery of any other craft,” he concluded.
Article Summary: Bryan Johnson has reignited a long-running public debate over his relationship with food. He wrote that he rejects being told he has an eating disorder, arguing instead that what critics see as pathology is actually years of disciplined mastery over what he eats. He questioned why that discipline gets labeled a disorder rather than celebrated as skill.

Article Title: Delhi University PhD scholar booked for slapping professor; CCTV captures attack
Article Text:
Delhi Police said CCTV footage showed Singh waiting for the professor before allegedly attacking him as he entered the building.

(With agency inputs)





NEW DELHI: Delhi University has suspended a PhD scholar and banned his entry into the university premises following an alleged assault on a professor at Umang Bhawan, officials said on Monday.According to news agency ANI, an FIR has been registered at Maurice Nagar police station, and a probe into the incident is underway, police said.The Delhi University Proctor’s Office said CCTV footage of the incident, which took place around 10:30 am at Umang Bhawan, showed alleged misconduct by Shubham Singh, a PhD scholar at the Faculty of Law who was admitted in the 2024-25 academic session (Phase-II).The university said Singh has been suspended from the Faculty of Law with immediate effect. He has also been barred from entering the University of Delhi premises under Ordinance XV-B of the Delhi University Act, 1922.Meanwhile, Delhi Police said CCTV footage showed Singh waiting for the professor before allegedly attacking him as he entered the building.The Democratic Teachers' Front (DTF) has also condemned the alleged assault on the Professor."The physical assault on a Professor by a research scholar at the Faculty of Law on August 17, 2026, is extremely concerning and demands urgent attention. The CCTV footage shows that the student was waiting and started beating the teacher as he was entering the building.As per the order of the Proctor dated August 17, 2026, the student involved in today's incident has been suspended. However, mere suspension does not address the gravity of this incident," DTF said in a statement.The Teachers' body noted that such incidents were repeatedly occuring on the campus.DTF stated, "Today's assault is not an isolated case. The safety and dignity of teachers on campus is being repeatedly compromised. Only recently, several professors at the Faculty of Law were verbally abused by a student in a separate incident. Last year, DUSU Joint Secretary Deepika Jha slapped a professor at Dr. Bhim Rao Ambedkar College.""The slow, insufficient and often absent response of the administration in such cases has left teachers with little confidence that the administration will act decisively when they are physically or verbally assaulted, abused and threatened. We demand that strict, swift action be taken against the student responsible in this case, and that the administration put in place clear, enforceable measures to prevent further attacks on teachers," the statement read.
Article Summary: Shubham Singh has been suspended from the Faculty of Law with immediate effect. Delhi Police said CCTV footage showed Singh waiting for the professor before allegedly attacking him as he entered the building. The Democratic Teachers' Front (DTF) has also condemned the alleged assault on the Professor.

Article Title: Twisha Sharma death by suicide, no sign of assault or struggle: AIIMS
Article Text:
The AIIMS board reviewed available national and international scientific literature before arriving at its conclusion.

‘Dispute over ligature material resolved’





NEW DELHI: An AIIMS medical board that conducted a court-ordered second postmortem of Twisha Sharma has concluded that she died by suicidal hanging and it did not find injuries of medico-legal importance suggestive of assault or struggle.“It is a clear case of suicide and there are no injuries of medico-legal importance suggestive of any physical assault, resistance or struggle on the body of the deceased, Twisha, prior to death,” said Dr Sudhir Gupta, head of department of forensic medicine at AIIMS, in a report submitted to CBI in sealed cover in compliance with MP HC’s order.The 11-page opinion prepared by a five-member team, which examined the death of Twisha from a “suicide or murder” prism, stressed that forensic experts had examined the case from all angles, including the disputed ligature material allegedly used for hanging, including a gymnastics belt with a metal ring.The AIIMS board reviewed available national and international scientific literature before arriving at its conclusion.Dr Gupta said the AIIMS board had resolved the dispute regarding the ligature material after examining available evidence.The board was constituted following a direction by HC ordering AIIMS to conduct a second postmortem examination, which was carried out on May 24, following which the board also visited the crime scene.Dr Gupta said the medical board deliberated on the case in detail and considered available national and international scientific literature for nearly a month before giving its final opinion.“It is a crystal-clear opinion for CBI and for the judiciary in the interest of truth and justice,” he said.
Article Summary: AIIMS medical board that conducted a court-ordered second postmortem of Twisha Sharma has concluded that she died by suicidal hanging. No injuries of medico- legal importance suggestive of any physical assault, resistance or struggle on the body of the deceased, Twisha, prior to death.

Article Title: DU suspends PhD scholar for attacking teacher, bans campus entry
Article Text: New Delhi: Delhi University has suspended a PhD scholar of its Faculty of Law for allegedly assaulting a teacher and banned his entry into the DU campus with immediate effect. The university has not specified the duration of the suspension.According to a notice issued by the proctor's office Monday, the incident took place around 10.30am at Umang Bhawan. According to a footage reviewed by the proctor's office before taking the decision, the scholar, a second-year PhD student admitted in the 2024-25 academic session (phase-II), allegedly slapped the faculty member Monday as he was entering the Law Centre building, causing him to fall. Several people gathered immediately and a security personnel were seen intervening.The footage showed the student engaging in a heated argument with the teacher and allegedly making repeated attempts to attack him as those present tried to de-escalate the situation. The reason for the altercation was not immediately known.The notice stated the scholar's entry into the DU premises had been banned under Ordinance XV-B of Delhi University Act, 1922.DU proctor Manoj Kumar told TOI that a proctorial inquiry would be constituted and further action would be taken based on its findings, which could include termination.The faculty member, who was part of the panel that interviewed the student for PhD admission last year, told TOI that he did not know the student beyond the interview. "He all of a sudden attacked me with slaps and punches. I fell down. He kept blabbering, ‘How dare you question me during the interview.' I don't know what triggered him," he said.The teacher said he underwent a medical examination and filed a police complaint.The student could not be contacted for a response.
Article Summary: Delhi University suspends PhD scholar for allegedly assaulting a teacher. Student allegedly slapped faculty member, causing him to fall. Incident took place around 10.30am at Umang Bhawan. Proctorial inquiry will be constituted and further action will be taken.

Article Title: Students protest outside NTA office after re-exam circular
Article Text:
New Delhi:





Student groups staged a protest outside NTA ’s office in Okhla Monday, demanding accountability from the agency after a recent circular called for re-examinations in three UGC-NET subjects. The re-test is scheduled to be conducted in three weeks.The circular states factual and grammatical errors in the question paper, as well as repetition of questions, as the reason for cancelling previously held sociology, english and commerce exams.“Was NTA sleeping when it allowed questions with grammatical errors to be used? Now it has suddenly woken up, two months after the exams were conducted,” said Sant Kumar, a PhD scholar from Jamia Millia Islamia.Protesters included online educators, who alleged that the sociology question paper had been leaked and had discrepancies, “but, the english and commerce questions were fine. Pressuring students by cancelling an exam only because previous year questions were repeated is unfair.”Protesters demand that NTA be scrapped as the nodal testing agency, re-exams be postponed and re-allocation of exam centres. Considering the toll competitive exams take on students, SFI member Sharanya Verma said, “Re-exams cannot be conducted in haste as students need time to prepare.Most of them have also returned to their homes. They should be allowed to choose whatever centre is nearby.”Around 100 protesting students tried to march into the NTA office, leading to a scuffle with police. Three police vans were brought in and over 50 students were reportedly detained to diffuse the situation. However, a senior cop said that police only removed protesters away from the gate of the complex, but no one was detained.“The fight will continue until a solution is reached,” said Aniket Madke, adding that the success of the CJP protest has encouraged them to fight for fair examinations.
Article Summary: Protesters demand that NTA be scrapped as the nodal testing agency, re-exams be postponed and re-allocation of exam centres. Around 100 protesting students tried to march into the NTA office, leading to a scuffle with police. Three police vans were brought in and over 50 students were reportedly detained.

Article Title: DUSU polls will be called off if campaign rules continue to be flouted, warns university
Article Text:
DU has warned candidates against using more than five cars in their campaign convoy or bringing luxury cars on the campus. (File photo)





NEW DELHI: Delhi University has warned that the DUSU elections would be called off if it keeps getting complaints that candidates were using more than five cars in their campaign convoy or were bringing luxury cars on the campus.The campaign has caused traffic jams and violence on the campus in the run-up to the polls.University officials met DUSU office-bearers, representatives of various student bodies and police officers Monday to review the arrangements and alleged violations.The meeting, where the ACP of north district, SHO of Maurice Nagar police station and a traffic inspector were present, was held at the proctor’s office.Addressing issues discussed at the previous meeting on July 16, the proctor issued a warning to student representatives over non-compliance with regulations laid down by the Delhi High Court and the Lyngdoh committee, saying this had resulted in “disorder on the university campus”.Officials flagged the use of luxury vehicles for election related activities and unauthorised parking by candidates along Chhatra Marg and University Road, which was causing traffic congestion.The guidelines issued after the meeting said that all candidates will be provided authorised vehicle stickers by the proctor’s office. Vehicles without these stickers will not be allowed to enter the university campus or any college.Candidates can park only in designated areas and not in a manner that obstructs traffic or inconveniences pedestrians.The university also prohibited the use of pamphlets or other printed material that could result in littering or damage to public property.The proctor warned that if a candidate or his/her supporters are found consuming alcohol or any intoxicating substance in a vehicle or anywhere on campus, including parking areas and roadsides, the candidate’s nomination would be cancelled.The university said any violation of the rules could lead to the cancellation of a candidate’s nomination. “The entire election may be cancelled” in case of violations, the proctor said.The university reiterated that all candidates, student organisations and other stakeholders must ensure that election activities are conducted in a peaceful and orderly manner.
Article Summary: DU has warned candidates against using more than five cars in their campaign convoy or bringing luxury cars on the campus. University officials met DUSU office-bearers, representatives of various student bodies and police officers Monday to review the arrangements and alleged violations.

Article Title: 'Nobody will be spared': FDA chief Tukaram Munde defends notices to SRK, Ajay Devgn, Tiger Shroff over Vimal ad
Article Text:
FDA commissioner Tukaram Mundhe defended actions against celebrities endorsing surrogate products.

Over 8,000 complaints resolved

FDA examining other advertisements

Action against excessive food additives





MUMBAI: Maharashtra Food and Drug Administration (FDA) Commissioner Tukaram Mundhe has defended action against celebrities endorsing surrogate products, saying everyone involved in creating, publishing or sponsoring advertisements is accountable under food safety regulations.The FDA recently issued a show-cause notice and a final warning to actors Shah Rukh Khan, Ajay Devgn and Tiger Shroff over their appearance in an advertisement for Vimal Elaichi. The department said the campaign prima facie amounted to indirect or surrogate promotion of prohibited pan masala and tobacco-related products.In an interview with news agency PTI, Mundhe said the advertisement was being examined as a possible surrogate advertisement, noting that the company had also been found selling gutkha in the past.“The issue is about Food Safety and Standards Regulations implementation. One of the regulations is about advertisement and misleading claims,” he said.Mundhe said the regulations, introduced in 2018 and effective from July 1, 2019, prohibit representations in physical, electronic, social media or other forms that state, imply or suggest claims that are untrue.Advertisers found violating these provisions would be issued notices and asked to explain why action should not be initiated against them, he said.“Everybody across the chain is responsible. It applies to all,” Mundhe said, urging those involved in advertising to familiarise themselves with FSSAI regulations governing advertisements and claims.Maharashtra has had a prohibitory order against gutkha, pan masala and related tobacco products since 2012, he said. The FDA is also cracking down on the smuggling and black marketing of prohibited tobacco products by registering FIRs, tracing their source and investigating links to companies and their directors.“Nobody is going to be spared, whether rural or urban. Those who sell, those who possess, those who process, those who manufacture, it is applicable to all,” he said.The department is also exploring the use of provisions under the organised crime law in such cases, Mundhe added.Mundhe said the FDA’s online complaints portal, complaints.myfda.in, has received more than 9,000 complaints since its launch, with over 8,000 resolved in about a month.“More than 8,000 complaints are resolved, and almost 700-800 are under process,” he said.The portal allows complainants to track the status of their complaints, while the department can monitor their progress. It also has features such as automatic accountability, assignment and escalation, he said.Citizens can also approach Mundhe directly during his designated 4 pm to 5 pm public interaction period.Mundhe said the FDA’s scrutiny was not limited to tobacco-related products. Advertisements for other products are also being examined, and action would be taken wherever misleading claims or other violations are found.“Whatever the product somebody is endorsing, they have to look into the guidelines and regulations of FSSAI about advertising and claims. If wrongfulness is found, we will take action against those also,” he said.Several products are currently under examination, though Mundhe declined to disclose details, saying the department’s action was part of a broader plan.“This is a part of a plan. I can't reveal it now and let the people know that I am taking action against a particular one at a particular time,” he said.The commissioner also said the FDA would strictly enforce regulations governing artificial colors and additives when they are used beyond permissible limits in bakeries, cakes, Chinese food and other products.“Additives regulations will be implemented strictly, and we are taking action against those, and some of the actions have already started,” he said.
Article Summary: The FDA recently issued a show-cause notice and a final warning to actors Shah Rukh Khan, Ajay Devgn and Tiger Shroff over their appearance in an advertisement for Vimal Elaichi. The department said the campaign prima facie amounted to indirect or surrogate promotion of prohibited pan masala and tobacco-related products.
